p01.title: The Gamecock (film)
p01.article: The Gamecock is a 1964 film directed by Pasquale Festa Campanile. It was one of his earlier directorial works. The film is a drama and is unrelated to any monster or creature feature.
p01.digest: The Gamecock is a 1964 drama film directed by Pasquale Festa Campanile, one of his earlier directorial works.

p02.title: Monster a Go-Go
p02.article: Monster a Go-Go is a 1965 American science fiction horror film directed by Bill Rebane and Herschell Gordon Lewis. The film concerns an astronaut who returns to Earth transformed into a monster.
p02.digest: Monster a Go-Go is a 1965 American science fiction horror film, directed by Bill Rebane and Herschell Gordon Lewis, about an astronaut who returns to Earth transformed into a monster.

p03.title: Pasquale Festa Campanile
p03.article: Pasquale Festa Campanile was an Italian film director, screenwriter and novelist. He was born on 28 July 1927 in Melfi, Italy, and died on 25 February 1986. He directed The Gamecock in 1964.
p03.digest: Pasquale Festa Campanile (1927–1986) was an Italian film director, screenwriter, and novelist, born in Melfi, whose directorial works include the 1964 film The Gamecock.

p04.title: Herschell Gordon Lewis
p04.article: Herschell Gordon Lewis was an American filmmaker often called the Godfather of Gore. He was born on 15 June 1926 in Chicago, Illinois, and died on 26 September 2016. He co-directed Monster a Go-Go.
p04.digest: Herschell Gordon Lewis (1926–2016) was an American filmmaker known as the "Godfather of Gore" and co-director of *Monster a Go-Go*.

p05.title: Bill Rebane
p05.article: Bill Rebane is an American film director born in 1937 in Riga, Latvia. He is best known for low-budget films and co-directed Monster a Go-Go with Herschell Gordon Lewis.
p05.digest: Bill Rebane is a Latvian-born American film director (born 1937) known for low-budget films, including the co-directed movie Monster a Go-Go.

p06.title: The Mask of the Gorilla
p06.article: The Mask of the Gorilla is a 1958 French crime film. It has no connection to Monster a Go-Go or The Gamecock and features no astronauts.
p06.digest: The Mask of the Gorilla is a 1958 French crime film, unrelated to Monster a Go-Go or The Gamecock and containing no astronauts.

p07.title: The Capture of Bigfoot
p07.article: The Capture of Bigfoot is a 1979 American horror film directed by Bill Rebane. It is about a legendary snow creature and is unrelated to The Gamecock.
p07.digest: The Capture of Bigfoot is a 1979 American horror film directed by Bill Rebane about a legendary snow creature.

p08.title: Monster from the Ocean Floor
p08.article: Monster from the Ocean Floor is a 1954 American science fiction film. It is often confused with other monster films of the era but has a distinct plot and crew.
p08.digest: Monster from the Ocean Floor is a distinct 1954 American science fiction film, often confused with other monster films of that era.

p09.title: John V, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst
p09.article: John V, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst was a German prince of the House of Ascania. He was born on 4 September 1504 in Dessau and died on 4 February 1551 in Zerbst. He was the son of Ernest I, Prince of Anhalt-Dessau. His eldest son was Karl I, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst.
p09.digest: John V, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst (1504–1551) was a German prince of the House of Ascania, son of Ernest I of Anhalt-Dessau and father of Karl I of Anhalt-Zerbst.

p10.title: Ernest I, Prince of Anhalt-Dessau
p10.article: Ernest I, Prince of Anhalt-Dessau was a German prince of the House of Ascania. He died on 12 June 1516 in Dessau. He was the father of John V, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst.
p10.digest: Ernest I, Prince of Anhalt-Dessau, was a German prince of the House of Ascania who died on 12 June 1516 in Dessau and was the father of John V, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst.

p11.title: Karl I, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst
p11.article: Karl I, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst was a German prince. He was the eldest son of John V, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst and succeeded to the principality of Anhalt-Zerbst.
p11.digest: Karl I was a German prince and the eldest son of John V, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst, whom he succeeded as ruler of the principality of Anhalt-Zerbst.

p12.title: Margarete of Munsterberg
p12.article: Margarete of Munsterberg was the daughter of Henry I, Duke of Munsterberg-Oels. She was the mother of John V, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst. This page is a distractor for questions about John V's father.
p12.digest: Margarete of Munsterberg, daughter of Henry I, Duke of Munsterberg-Oels, was the mother of John V, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst.

p13.title: House of Ascania
p13.article: The House of Ascania was a dynasty of German rulers. Members included princes of Anhalt-Dessau and Anhalt-Zerbst. It is a broad category page and does not by itself state individual birth or death dates.
p13.digest: The House of Ascania was a German ruling dynasty whose members included the princes of Anhalt-Dessau and Anhalt-Zerbst.

p14.title: Joachim I Nestor, Elector of Brandenburg
p14.article: Joachim I Nestor was Elector of Brandenburg. His daughter Margaret of Brandenburg married John V, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst. He is unrelated to the film questions.
p14.digest: This passage identifies Joachim I Nestor as Elector of Brandenburg, noting that his daughter Margaret married John V, Prince of Anhalt-Zerbst, and states he is unrelated to the film questions.

p15.title: Godfather of Gore
p15.article: The Godfather of Gore is a nickname associated with Herschell Gordon Lewis for his splatter films. This page is about the nickname and does not itself list birth dates.
p15.digest: This passage explains that "Godfather of Gore" is a nickname for filmmaker Herschell Gordon Lewis, known for his splatter films, and notes the page does not contain birth date information.

p16.title: Melfi
p16.article: Melfi is a town in the Basilicata region of southern Italy. It is the birthplace of the film director Pasquale Festa Campanile. This page is a geographic distractor.
p16.digest: Melfi is a town in the Basilicata region of southern Italy, notable as the birthplace of film director Pasquale Festa Campanile.
